beats.title: Incoming Transmission: What Is the Amalgaverse?
beats.headline: THE AMALGAVERSE
beats.text:
THE AMALGAVERSE 

Launches Monday, September 21st at 12:01 p.m. ET🚀

1. What is the Amalgaverse?

The Amalgaverse is a shared sandbox of fictional SF universes that will serve as the setting for a series of missions that will play out as episodic adventures in the style of the beloved ship-based sci-fi shows of the 90's.

2. How will these missions play out?

The missions will play out in the form of an online choose-your-own-adventure format with fan voting driving the narrative.  YOU choose the missions.  YOU select the away teams.  YOU make the decisions that shape each adventure.  For instance, initially you will be given four missions to choose from. Depending on which one you choose, you’ll be presented with a scenario – a damaged ship, a space station, a planet – and may be asked how you intend to get there. Maybe you like to fly in on the jumper. Maybe you’d rather try an EVA. Or perhaps you’d prefer to just directly beam aboard. Then, who is on your away team? Which corridor will you turn down? How will you react to the threat? And so on. Whatever course of action you choose will inform the next step.

3. In what capacity will I be making these decisions?

Sometimes, you will be deciding as yourself, our 20th crew member. Sometimes, you will be deciding on behalf of any of your fellow crew members. Still other times, you will be deciding on behalf of the crew as a whole.

4. What happens if we make a decision that goes against the plot you had in mind?

Each adventure has multiple paths and subplots. Your vote directs which one we follow. There is no single “correct” route, and mission success is NOT guaranteed.

5. I’m at work all day. Will I miss it?

No. I’ll be updating every step of our adventure daily at 12:01 p.m. E.T. The fandom will have 24 hours to weigh in and decide on a course of action. Majority rules.
Every update will be pinned at the top of my timeline. Just please be sure to turn on notifications so you don’t miss the most recent posts.

6. Can I jump in mid-mission, or do I have to wait for the next episode?"

Jump in anytime. Every post contains a recap to get you up to speed immediately. You don’t need to have voted on day one to weigh in on day twelve.

7. Will you be using X’s polling feature to count votes?

No, for two equally valid reasons. First, X won’t let me include both a visual AND a poll in a dedicated post, and the visual matters more to me. Second, I don’t want to just know HOW you vote, I want to know WHY you vote a certain way. Your overall reasoning will also factor into how your mission plays out.

8. Will you be offering a summary with each update?

Yes. Every new installment will open with a short “story so far,” then a more detailed summary in the second part of that same post. Each installment will also quote-tweet the previous one, so you can walk the full chain if you want every beat.

9. How long will each adventure run?

3-4 weeks. They have been structured like a television episode – 5 acts, with roughly 5 beats (decision points) per act. Each mission should feel like you’re experiencing a classic sci-fi t.v. episode.  Just like old times!

10. Will the choices we make carry forward into future missions?

Yes. If you lose the F-302, the puddle jumper, or a crew member over the course of a mission, they will be lost for future missions. Your choices will have consequences.

11. How many missions have you designed?

Since these missions will play out like episodes from those beloved ship-based sci-fi shows of the 90's, I've structured a similar rollout.  Ten missions to start followed by a brief hiatus after which the back half ten episodes will unfold.  20 missions/episodes in total.  That will be our first season.  And depending on fan response, a second season could be in the cards.

12.  Will you be offering a summary of each adventure once complete?

Not at launch.

13. This seems like a lot of work.  Why are you doing this?

I'm tired of crafting stories (pitches, pilots scripts, series bibles) that never see the light of day, always subject to the whims of gormless executives.  Science fiction is a tough sell.  Far future sci-fi, tougher still.  Far future ship-based sci-fi, toughest of all.  But that's my jam.  And I've missed it.  So this allows me to do what I do best, exercise those creative muscles, and hopefully give SF fans something to look forward to with every mission.  For entertainment purposes only of course.

14. But, characters aside, couldn't you just turn these stories into a script you can try selling or a book you could publish?  Wouldn't that be more lucrative?

Sure, in theory. But the odds of selling far-future, ship-based sci-fi right now are microscopic, and I’d rather actually make something people can experience today than stick another finished script in a digital drawer. As for a novel? That’s a massive solitary grind. This is fast, interactive, and fun.

15. Will there be guest stars throughout?

I’m concentrating on this crew first. Guest appearances are possible later.

16. I get motion sick. Should I worry?

No. The ship has inertial dampers. The ride will be smoother than a luxury liner.

17. Okay, enough questions.  When do we get started?

The adventures begin Monday, September 21st at 12:01 p.m. E.T., here on X.  Set a reminder and turn on notifications so you don't miss a beat!

beats.text:
The #Amalgaverse begins!

You’re just finishing up lunch, considering that last cookie on the counter when, suddenly, you are assailed by a blinding flash.

Vertigo.  Pitch blackness.  A few seconds of incoherence.

Then, when you awaken, you find yourself transported to an alternate universe, a far future where the Federation, Galactic Empire, Earth Alliance, Twelve Colonies, and many other factions vie for power.

An elite ship is commissioned and an equally elite crew formed, comprised of the very best of myriad realities, every one of them stranded - like you - in this amalgam setting.  Their mission: to explore this strange new multi-universe, to seek out new clues and answers to their cosmic quandary, to boldly go - and figure out a way for everyone to get back home.

19 incredible crew members.  And...you!  Yes, you have been chosen as the all-important 20th member due to your encyclopedic knowledge of these multiple realities.  Back on your Earth, they are mere fiction, beloved television shows, but here (and back in their realities), they are real.  And YOU possess the knowledge that unites them!

So your first choice is this.  Do you set your phasers, zats, force lances, and Peacekeeper pulse pistols to fun and join the Alt. Enterprise-D and its crew on their maiden voyage?

Yes/No

Choose!

votes.headline: Crew votes overwhelmingly to sign aboard the Alt. Enterprise-D

reasons.yes: Most crew embraced the adventure outright, eager for orders, warp speed, and whatever chaos awaited.
reasons.no: The small holdout balked mainly over an interrupted snack, not the mission itself.

votes.wildcards: A missing cookie dominated sentiment across both camps, with several holdouts reversing course once reassured replicators could produce a replacement.

beats.title: Four Contacts, One Ship
beats.headline: Choose your first  mission!
beats.question: Four crises. One ship. No back-up. Where do we set course first?

options.label: Contact One — The Ghost Ship
options.summary: A derelict vessel cycling a fragmented Federation distress call. No lights, no drive, no life signs.

options.label: Contact Two — The Heist
options.summary: A Ferengi shadow auction for Artifact Omicron-8 — possibly an outlawed subspace weapon.

options.label: Contact Three — The Delivery
options.summary: Extract intelligence broker Harven Zax, wanted by Romulans, the Orion Syndicate and a Klingon Great House.

options.label: Contact Four — The Fracture
options.summary: Kirin Station Outpost Gamma-3 has gone silent. 23 crew. No beacon. No debris.

beats.text:
Choose your first #Amalgaverse mission!

Captain's Log - Stargate Unknown: I have commanded starships through Klingon ambushes, Romulan incursions across the Neutral Zone, and temporal anomalies that would unsettle lesser officers, but none of it prepared me for this.  The Enterprise-D has been refitted, re-crewed with the finest officers from across multiple realities, and given a new mission: explore this strange new universe, and find a way to get everyone home.

The hum of the warp core fades as the Enterprise-D drops out of warp, and the star field ahead resolves from streaking lights into cold, fixed points.  Ops reports four near-simultaneous contacts within  the first ninety seconds of arrival.  

CONTACT ONE - A subspace signal, heavily degraded, cycling on the Federation emergency frequency but fragmented beyond standard universal translation resolution.  It's coming from bearing 227 mark 14, approximately 350,000 kilometers off the port bow.  Long-range sensors confirm  vessel drifting cold - no running lights, no drive signature, no signs of life.  (The Ghost Ship)

CONTACT TWO - A scrambled tight-beam transmission interception by the communications array, passing through this sector on an encrypted Ferengi commercial channel.  Ops has partially decoded the manifest: a shadow auction for Artifact Omicron-8, provenance heavily redacted.  Its appended energy signature matches no commercial technology on record.  It reads, partially and imperfectly, like an illicit subspace weapon outlawed under the Khitomer Accords.  (The Heist) 
 
CONTACT THREE - Starfleet priority channel, addressed directly to Captain Kirk.  Locate and extract Harven Zax, a dangerous intelligence broker, currently aboard a disabled Vespian cruiser at coordinates 188 mark 44, and deliver him to a rendezvous point at the edge of the Expanse within seventy-two hours.  He is wanted, arguably, dead or alive, by three different groups: the Romulans, the Orion Syndicate, and a Klingon Great House.  (The Delivery)   

CONTACT FOUR - A lateral sensor sweep reports a complete absence of subspace comm traffic from Kirin Station Outpost Gamma-3, a Federation research installation on the Expanse's rim.  Gamma-3 has a crew of twenty-three and files automated status reports every four hours.  The last confirmed report is sixty-three hours old.  The station's emergency beacon is not active.  There is no debris field.  Simply... silence.  (The Fracture)   

The bridge is dead quiet.

Four crises.  One ship.  No back-up.

You must decide where we set course first.  

What say you? 

Choose! 

And cue our Opening Theme...

recap.text:
Previously On...#Amalgaverse

You and 19 others have been stranded in an amalgam universe of myriad SF realities.  All 19 are sci-fi's Best of the Best.  And then there's you, uniquely qualified given your encyclopedic knowledge garnered from your world where these characters, their technologies, and their stories are fiction, beloved t.v. shows you have watched time and again.  Together, all 20 of you have set off on the Enterprise-D, tasked with finding a way home.

votes.headline: Fleet answers the mayday: Ghost Ship wins, Fracture close behind

reasons.ghost: Maritime instinct won out — a mayday from a nearby vessel could not be ignored, whatever the risk.
reasons.fracture: Twenty-three silent researchers on a known outpost made this feel like the most urgent life-at-stake call.
reasons.delivery: A Starfleet priority channel addressed straight to the captain read as a direct order that outranked the rest.
reasons.heist: Curiosity about a black-market weapon and a shot at outrunning the Ferengi made this the fun, high-stakes pick.

votes.wildcards: Recurring debate over whether Starfleet orders or the old law of the sea should set the tiebreaker, plus a fair number hoping to split the ship and chase two crises at once.

beats.title: How Do We Get Aboard?
beats.headline: First Mission: The Ghost Ship (Part 1)
beats.question: A derelict freighter sits inside a pulsing spatial anomaly. Whose advice do you follow?

options.label: Scotty — beam aboard
options.summary: Transport straight to the bridge in a lull between pulses. Fast — but extraction may not be instant.

options.label: Sheppard — fly the jumper in
options.summary: Park the puddle jumper in the open hangar bay for a clean getaway. Long hike to the bridge.

options.label: Garak — enter via the hull breach
options.summary: Jumper, then EVA through the rupture midway between bridge and hangar. Slow, exposed, unexpected.

options.label: McKay — skip this one
options.summary: "The three worst ideas since the Matrix sequels." Don't board at all.

beats.text:
First Mission: The Ghost Ship (Part 1)
#Amalgaverse 

Captain’s Log, supplemental. We've answered a distress call at the coordinates flagged by our long-range sensors, and found a ship gone silent. Automated beacon still cycling, running lights dark, and no one responding to our hails.

A freighter drifts before you, drive cold, cycling a fragmented distress call on a loop. The ship sits at the heart of a spatial anomaly venting irregular pulses of raw energy.

You’re going aboard. The only question is how.

Scotty offers to beam the away team aboard in a lull between the anomaly’s pulses. It’s the quickest way in and puts everyone directly on the freighter’s bridge. But the pulses are intermittent, and he warns: “If ye have to leave in a hurry, I’ll move heaven and earth to pull ye back, but I canna swear it’ll be the very second ye shout for it.”

Sheppard pitches flying the puddle jumper straight into the freighter’s hangar bay, where they can park it for a clean getaway. The bay is open to space and it’s also a ways from the bridge, but John will take that trade: “Sure, it’s a bit of a hike, but I’d still sooner have the jumper at my back if things go sideways.”

Garak favors accessing the ship through a hull breach that sits at the midpoint between the bridge and the hangar. Take the jumper, then enter through the rupture by EVA. Garak nevertheless admits: “It’s slow going, leaves you terribly exposed, and yes, it could get everyone killed. Which is why it’s the one approach someone who may be on board would least expect. And in my experience, the only arrival worth arranging is the one no one thought to prepare for.”

McKay isn’t a fan of any of these options. He points out: “Two involve open vacuum and the third requires us to be reduced to a data stream in the immediate vicinity of an unquantified spatial anomaly. These are the three worst ideas since the Matrix sequels!” He suggests skipping this one.

Whose advice do you follow?

Choose!

votes.headline: Sheppard's jumper run wins decisively over beaming and the breach

reasons.sheppard: Crew favored keeping a physical ship nearby for extraction and a chance to scout the freighter en route to the bridge.
reasons.scotty: Backers trusted transporter speed and Scotty's track record, often pairing it with the jumper as a standby rescue option.
reasons.garak: This faction liked the element of surprise and using the hull breach for reconnaissance before anyone knew they'd boarded.
reasons.mckay: Risk-averse voters argued the mission wasn't worth it and favored remote scans or handing it off entirely.

votes.wildcards: Recurring gags included dread over transporter mishaps, McKay's chronic cowardice being both mocked and grudgingly respected, and several crews trying to split the difference by sending two teams at once.

beats.title: The Hangar Doors
beats.headline: First Mission: The Ghost Ship (Part 1)
beats.question: The hangar doors are jammed open to space. Whose advice do you take?

options.label: Rommie — crank them shut by hand
options.summary: Her android frame handles vacuum. Slow and exposed — and the anomaly's pulses could knock her offline.

beats.text:
First Mission: The Ghost Ship (Part 1)  #Amalgaverse 

You've decided to investigate a seemingly derelict freighter broadcasting an emergency beacon.

O’Neill shuttles the rest of the away team - Daniel Jackson, Rommie, and Rodney McKay - to the ghost ship, threading the jumper into the open bay and setting down inside.  “Just like riding a bike,”he says with some satisfaction.  “A twenty-six-foot-long, fifteen-and-a-half-foot-wide bike with forward-mounted drone launchers and a cloak.”

But you quickly realize there’s a problem.  The hangar doors are jammed open to space, and won’t cycle shut.  What’s your next move?

Rommie suggests forcing the doors shut manually.  Her android frame handles extended vacuum without a problem, so she can just walk out and crank them closed by hand.  It’s slow and exposed, but the sure fix.  “The catch isn’t the vacuum,”she adds.  “It’s the anomaly.  Those energy pulses hit while I’m out there, and they could knock me offline before the job’s done."  And then, catching Daniel staring: “What?”  Daniel pops his eyebrows, considering: “Nothing.  You just remind me of someone."

McKay pitches running a hard line from the jumper to the dead servos.  It will power the doors shut, but potentially bleed some of the jumper’s reserves.  “Potentially?”asks O’Neill.  “Potentially - possible,”he non-commits.  “More or less.  Ish."

O’Neill considers just leaving the bay open and heading in directly through the interior airlock given they’re already wearing EV suits.  "We're dressed for the occasion."  It’s the fastest way in, but their ride ends up parked inside an airless bay, so any retreat means crossing vacuum again.

Whose advice do you take?

Choose!
